overview.text: Today's developments center on agent learning environments, scene text editing data, multi-team credit assignment, and infrastructure growth. First, researchers are tackling the challenge of agent world model synthesis to safely scale learning outside real-world computer systems. Second, new approaches to scene text editing focus purely on real data to preserve original styles without paired synthetic training pipelines. Third, cooperative language-model teams are improving through group-relative credit assignment that traces shared team rewards back to individual agents and skills. Finally, broader industry trends show massive data center acceleration alongside expanding commercial footprints like ChatGPT Ads reaching new countries and ongoing discussions around model safety policy and governance standards.

entries.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
entries.summary: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks.
entries.why: Enables safe agent learning by synthesizing computer-use environments without real-world security risks.

entries.title: Real In, Real Out: What If We Only Use Real Data for Scene Text Editing?
entries.summary: Aiming to modify textual content while preserving the original style, Scene Text Editing (STE) has significant practical value in many applications. STE typically requires paired images before and after editing for training.
entries.why: Simplifies scene text editing by relying entirely on real data instead of paired training images.

entries.title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
entries.summary: Cooperative language-model agents can improve without weight updates by revising reusable skills, but only if a shared team reward is traced to the responsible agent and skill.
entries.why: Improves cooperative agent teams by accurately tracing shared team rewards to individual skills.

entries.title: Unsupervised Tool Evolution for Coding Agents in Data-Lake Analytics
entries.summary: Coding agents can answer analytical questions over a data lake by discovering, cleaning, and joining the relevant data. However, they discard this work after each question and redo it from scratch for the next one.
entries.why: Addresses data-lake analytics efficiency by letting coding agents evolve and retain tools across questions.

entries.title: Good Judgment, Bad Advice: Decision-Model Controllers Raise Agent Cost Without Improving Success
entries.summary: Agent scaffolds increasingly delegate small decisions (whether to stop, verify, or change approach) to cheaper models.
entries.why: Examines how delegating small decisions to cheaper controllers affects agent success and cost.

entries.title: Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents
entries.summary: Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents increasingly act over streaming omni-modal observations spanning screenshots, audio, video, interaction history, and device states.
entries.why: Explores GUI agents operating effectively over streaming omni-modal observations and device states.
